findings.message: `CliClient.call` accepts `on_event` (providers.py:336), but the driver reaches it only through `LLMEffect._call`, which invokes `self._llm.call(req)` against the `LLM` Protocol. That Protocol (llm.py:62) and `FakeLLM.call` (llm.py:95) take only `req`. Passing the detector through the effect means changing the Protocol and the fake, and squatch/llm.py is neither fenced nor in Context. The only in-fence alternative is a conditional kwarg, which is the dual-path code CLAUDE.md forbids.
findings.paved_road: Add squatch/llm.py to both the fence and Context, and state the single callback contract for the `LLM` Protocol and `FakeLLM`. Otherwise, bind the detector at `CliClient` construction in the composition roots so `LLM.call(req)` stays unchanged, and rewrite the scope and criteria to say so.

findings.message: `_RequisitionEffect.call` calls `LLMEffect._call.__wrapped__` directly with a fixed keyword set. Any change the ticket makes to `LLMEffect._call`'s signature to carry the callback breaks this module, which is outside the fence. Requisition review is also a production LLM call path, so leaving it out contradicts 'every production driver call, including review'.
findings.paved_road: Fence squatch/requisition.py and add it to Context. Alternatively, choose a construction-time binding that leaves the `LLMEffect._call` signature untouched, and say explicitly whether requisition review is in or out of scope.

findings.message: `LLMEffect`/`CliClient` are also composed in squatch/author.py, squatch/triage.py, squatch/requisition.py, and eval/ (diagnose, harness, shakeout bench, providers_group). The fence covers only stages/drain/serve/__main__. The criterion 'every production driver call ... is watched' therefore either forces edits to the unfenced author, triage, and requisition roots, or cannot be met.
findings.paved_road: Either fence squatch/author.py, squatch/triage.py, and squatch/requisition.py as production composition roots and list them as on-demand exceptions, or narrow the Goal and criteria to the Stages-owned Driver on the drain and serve paths and file the remaining production roots as a follow-up. Name the eval/ composers explicitly as non-production callers that keep the optional-callback behavior.
